55:26.en: Everyone upon the earth will perish

55:27.ar: وَيَبۡقَىٰ وَجۡهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلۡجَلَٰلِ وَٱلۡإِكۡرَامِ
55:27.en: And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor

50:19.ar: وَجَآءَتۡ سَكۡرَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنتَ مِنۡهُ تَحِيدُ
50:19.en: And the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid

3:185.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ فَمَن زُحۡزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ فَقَدۡ فَازَۗ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
3:185.en: Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your [full] compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion

39:30.en: Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die

21:34.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا لِبَشَرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ ٱلۡخُلۡدَۖ أَفَإِيْن مِّتَّ فَهُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِدُونَ
21:34.en: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die - would they be eternal

7:34.ar: وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ أَجَلࣱۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمۡ لَا يَسۡتَأۡخِرُونَ سَاعَةࣰ وَلَا يَسۡتَقۡدِمُونَ
7:34.en: And for every nation is a [specified] term. So when their time has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it]

jZh9J0tkzl4.title: Tazkiyah Halaqa: Mortality, Episode 23
jZh9J0tkzl4.one_line: Mortality is a gift, not a curse: accepting that life ends makes every moment valuable, present and urgent.
jZh9J0tkzl4.summary: Continuing the mortality pillar of his tazkiyah series, he separates death, a single unknown moment that is always a loss because it ends the chance to improve, from mortality, the fact that we are finite, which he calls a gift from Allah. Accepting mortality begins with sadness and moves through the stages of grief, just as reality in marriage differs from what men imagine; holding onto the illusion causes misery, while accepting reality opens a better life. Finite things are valuable and infinite things are not, so limited time creates urgency and beauty. He offers a hypothesis that Allah places us in a finite world first so we can appreciate the eternal life He offers later, and supports the idea with novels about immortality that always reintroduce death. The Prophet lived fully in each moment because he valued it. He describes walking out alive from a Syrian detention facility in 2013 as the only survivor, and warns against the psychology of exempting ourselves from what befalls others. He asks the audience to stop hiding death in a blind spot, to count the visits left with aging parents, to drop the word 'later', and to be present in prayer and with loved ones.

outline.heading: Mortality as the pillar that holds tazkiyah together
outline.gist: Of the five pillars of tazkiyah, removing mortality or resurrection makes the whole equation collapse.

outline.heading: What the Quran says about death
outline.gist: Everything on earth perishes except Allah; death comes to you, it is what you tried to avoid, and every soul will taste it. Even the Prophet was told he would die.

outline.heading: Hadith on remembering death
outline.gist: The Prophet wept at a grave and told the companions to prepare; the smartest people remember death most and prepare for it, and remembering it in hardship eases it.

outline.heading: Death versus mortality
outline.gist: Death is an undefined moment and always a negative; mortality is the fact of being finite, and making peace with it is how you take death seriously.

outline.heading: Why death itself is a loss
outline.gist: At death the chance to repent, improve and draw closer to Allah ends, so you want life to end well, but mortality is the opposite of this loss.

outline.heading: Acceptance begins with grief
outline.gist: Accepting mortality brings sadness and the stages of denial, anger, bargaining and depression before acceptance, as with any gap between imagination and reality.

outline.heading: Example: marriage as imagined versus real
outline.gist: Men who insist marriage match the picture in their heads make themselves and their wives miserable; those who accept it as it is can enjoy it.

outline.heading: Our delusional view of mortality
outline.gist: We avoid the topic, so our view is delusional; accepting that every moment brings us closer to the end is sad at first but changes how we experience life.

outline.heading: Finitude creates urgency
outline.gist: If we were immortal nothing would ever need doing now; limited time that cannot be extended makes urgency the centre of existence.

outline.heading: Finite things are valuable
outline.gist: Infinite resources lose value; water and clean air became precious only once they seemed scarce.

outline.heading: Why Allah gave a finite life before eternity
outline.gist: His hypothesis: the worldly part of us cannot appreciate abundance, just as a child given everything becomes spoiled and unloved.

outline.heading: Time is the one thing you cannot buy
outline.gist: Gold, clothing and houses can be replaced but not time, and here rich and poor are equal.

outline.heading: Living finitely to appreciate Paradise
outline.gist: Eternal life offered to someone who never knew mortality would go unthanked, so we live a finite life first to value what Allah will give.

outline.heading: Hiding death in a blind spot
outline.gist: We watch people fall off the cliff daily, attend janazahs, then go back to not thinking about it to avoid sadness.

outline.heading: Choosing between illusion and truth
outline.gist: Either keep living through a corrupt lens or absorb the sadness and live life truthfully, which is far better on the other side.

outline.heading: The Prophet lived in the moment
outline.gist: He enjoyed life deeply and worried little about his own future, teaching that food for tonight and a place to sleep is enough.

outline.heading: Counting the visits left with aging parents
outline.gist: Seeing a parent monthly for ten years is only 120 visits; knowing the number makes each meeting more beautiful and worth enjoying.

outline.heading: Novels of immortality always bring death back
outline.gist: Every novel series imagining human immortality ends with mortality reintroduced, because existence without end has no meaning.

outline.heading: Every breath beautified
outline.gist: The best gift about your time is that it ends, so each breath, meeting and prayer gains value.

outline.heading: Midlife crisis as a crisis of delusion
outline.gist: People who ignored mortality hit a crisis when their bodies decline and often do something foolish they regret.

outline.heading: In a hundred years no one here will remain
outline.gist: A century is short; everyone in the room will be gone, and accepting this brings sadness first.

outline.heading: Acceptance brings peace and gratitude for being alive
outline.gist: Once the sadness sinks in, it brings peace and appreciation that you are still here to breathe, learn, hope and love.

outline.heading: The Prophet fully present with family
outline.gist: He played with his grandchildren for hours and was wholly with whoever he sat with, because he valued the moment.

outline.heading: Distraction in prayer
outline.gist: Waiting for salah or a session to end comes from not valuing the present; wandering thoughts are anxiety that achieves nothing.

outline.heading: Imagine it is your last
outline.gist: Treating a moment as your last intensifies living; the companions saw death often and needed few reminders.

outline.heading: Professional distance versus exempting yourself
outline.gist: Detachment is needed to serve patients, but applying it to your own mortality is a mistake.

outline.heading: Death is the only certainty
outline.gist: Nothing else in life is guaranteed; everyone here will be buried and forgotten within a week.

outline.heading: Lessons from near-death experiences
outline.gist: Survivors live better for a while, and keep that quality only if they keep contemplating their mortality.

outline.heading: His survival of a Syrian detention facility
outline.gist: He walked out alive in April 2013 as the only survivor; his priorities changed completely until the effect wore off years later, and he treats his life as extra time.

outline.heading: The psychology of exemption
outline.gist: We protect ourselves by assuming disasters seen elsewhere will not happen to us, to avoid feeling vulnerable.

outline.heading: Never say 'that would not be me'
outline.gist: Claiming you could never be the addict or the afflicted is arrogance; you control none of the variables, so praise Allah for where you are.

outline.heading: Mortality brings humility
outline.gist: Internalising mortality also brings humbleness and pragmatism to everyday life.

outline.heading: No more 'later'
outline.gist: Accepting mortality removes procrastination in your relationship with Allah, your deen and your loved ones, because 'later' banks on a certainty you lack.

outline.heading: What accepting mortality gives you
outline.gist: It beautifies and intensifies life, brings peace and motivation; time is the one thing you cannot get refunded, yet using it well includes sitting with tea and taking in beauty.

outline.heading: Mortality as a gift, to be argued further
outline.gist: Living the moment intensely and using time well is what mortality offers; he promises more arguments next week.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Distinguishes death from mortality and argues finitude is a gift that gives life value.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: Time is the one resource that cannot be bought, so its limit creates urgency.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: Mortality removes the word 'later' and makes wasting time a crime.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Allah gives a finite life first so we can appreciate the eternal life He offers.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: The Prophet enjoyed life deeply and was fully present with family and companions.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: He played with his grandchildren for hours, never in a hurry to be elsewhere.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Counting remaining visits with aging parents makes each one precious.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Distraction in prayer comes from not valuing the present moment.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Exempting yourself from others' misfortune is arrogance; mortality brings humility.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Choose truthful acceptance over a comfortable illusion about death.

quran.point: Everything on earth perishes and only Allah remains.
The intoxication of death comes in truth; it is what you tried to avoid.
Every soul will taste death, repeated three times in the Quran.
The Prophet will die and so will they.
No human before him was given immortality.
Every nation has a term; when it comes there is no delay.

hadith.gist: The Prophet sat at the edge of a grave and wept until his tears fell, then told his brothers to prepare for this moment.
Asked who is the smartest of people, the Prophet said those who remember death most and prepare best for it.
Remember often the destroyer of pleasures; no one remembers it in hardship except that it eases it.
Whoever has food for his day and a safe place to sleep has been given the world.

maxims: Mortality is a gift, not a curse
Infinite things don't have value
The best gift about your time is that it ends
You cannot buy time
There's no later

stories.who: His detention in Syria, April 2013
stories.point: Surviving when everyone else died reset his priorities; he treats his life since as extra time to use well.

stories.who: Novels about human immortality
stories.point: Every such story ends by reintroducing death, showing endless existence has no meaning.

stories.who: The spoiled child
stories.point: Unlimited access breeds lack of appreciation, which is why we first experience a finite world.

contemporary: Syrian detention facilities during the war
takeaways: Stop hiding death in a blind spot; let the sadness of accepting mortality run its course
Count the visits you have left with aging parents and treat each as precious
Drop the word 'later' for repentance, deen and family ties
Be fully present in prayer and with loved ones instead of waiting for the next thing
Never say 'that would never be me' about others' trials

31:29.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِيٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ى وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
31:29.en: Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term, and that Allah, with whatever you do, is Acquainted

31:30.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡكَبِيرُ
31:30.en: That is because Allah is the Truth, and that what they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand

31:31.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِنِعۡمَتِ ٱللَّهِ لِيُرِيَكُم مِّنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّكُلِّ صَبَّارࣲ شَكُورࣲ‏
31:31.en: Do you not see that ships sail through the sea by the favor of Allah that He may show you of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful

31:32.ar: وَإِذَا غَشِيَهُم مَّوۡجࣱ كَٱلظُّلَلِ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخۡلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡبَرِّ فَمِنۡهُم مُّقۡتَصِدࣱۚ وَمَا يَجۡحَدُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِلَّا كُلُّ خَتَّارࣲ كَفُورࣲ‏
31:32.en: And when waves come over them like canopies, they supplicate Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, there are [some] of them who are moderate [in faith]. And none rejects Our signs except everyone treacherous and ungrateful

31:33.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡاْ يَوۡمࣰ ا لَّا يَجۡزِي وَالِدٌ عَن وَلَدِهِۦ وَلَا مَوۡلُودٌ هُوَ جَازٍ عَن وَالِدِهِۦ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّۖ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
31:33.en: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and be not deceived about Allah by the Deceiver

31:34.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡغَيۡثَ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسࣱ مَّاذَا تَكۡسِبُ غَدࣰ اۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسُۢ بِأَيِّ أَرۡضࣲ تَمُوتُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرُۢ
31:34.en: Indeed, Allah [alone] has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul perceives in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted

31:21.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَا وَجَدۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ يَدۡعُوهُمۡ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
31:21.en: And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has revealed," they say, "Rather, we will follow that upon which we found our fathers." Even if Satan was inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze

31:22.ar: ۞وَمَن يُسۡلِمۡ وَجۡهَهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحۡسِنࣱ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡأُمُورِ
31:22.en: And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good - then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to Allah will be the outcome of [all] matters

16:58.ar: وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِٱلۡأُنثَىٰ ظَلَّ وَجۡهُهُۥ مُسۡوَدࣰّ ا وَهُوَ كَظِيمࣱ‏
16:58.en: And when one of them is informed of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief

16:59.ar: يَتَوَٰرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ مِن سُوٓءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِۦٓۚ أَيُمۡسِكُهُۥ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمۡ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِي ٱلتُّرَابِۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَحۡكُمُونَ
16:59.en: He hides himself from the people because of the ill of which he has been informed. Should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the ground? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide

7:171.ar: ۞وَإِذۡ نَتَقۡنَا ٱلۡجَبَلَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُۥ ظُلَّةࣱ وَظَنُّوٓاْ أَنَّهُۥ وَاقِعُۢ بِهِمۡ خُذُواْ مَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةࣲ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
7:171.en: And [mention] when We raised the mountain above them as if it was a dark cloud and they were certain that it would fall upon them, [and Allah said], "Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it that you might fear Allah

53:26.ar: ۞وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لَا تُغۡنِي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن يَأۡذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرۡضَىٰٓ
53:26.en: And how many angels there are in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except [only] after Allah has permitted [it] to whom He wills and approves

11:42.ar: وَهِيَ تَجۡرِي بِهِمۡ فِي مَوۡجࣲ كَٱلۡجِبَالِ وَنَادَىٰ نُوحٌ ٱبۡنَهُۥ وَكَانَ فِي مَعۡزِلࣲ يَٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
11:42.en: And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son who was apart [from them], "O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers

11:43.ar: قَالَ سَـَٔاوِيٓ إِلَىٰ جَبَلࣲ يَعۡصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِۚ قَالَ لَا عَاصِمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا مَن رَّحِمَۚ وَحَالَ بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡمَوۡجُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُغۡرَقِينَ
11:43.en: [But] he said, "I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water." [Noah] said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He gives mercy." And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned

11:44.ar: وَقِيلَ يَٰٓأَرۡضُ ٱبۡلَعِي مَآءَكِ وَيَٰسَمَآءُ أَقۡلِعِي وَغِيضَ ٱلۡمَآءُ وَقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ وَٱسۡتَوَتۡ عَلَى ٱلۡجُودِيِّۖ وَقِيلَ بُعۡدࣰ ا لِّلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
11:44.en: And it was said, "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]." And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on the [mountain of] Judiyy. And it was said, "Away with the wrongdoing people

11:45.ar: وَنَادَىٰ نُوحࣱ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبۡنِي مِنۡ أَهۡلِي وَإِنَّ وَعۡدَكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحۡكَمُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
11:45.en: And Noah called to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family; and indeed, Your promise is true; and You are the most just of judges

11:46.ar: قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيۡسَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيۡرُ صَٰلِحࣲۖ فَلَا تَسۡـَٔلۡنِ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۖ إِنِّيٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
11:46.en: He said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so ask Me not for that about which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant

sa0db2ODNmo.speaker: adnan
sa0db2ODNmo.speaker_note: continues his own Sunday Arabic tafsir of Surat Luqman from last week
sa0db2ODNmo.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Luqman 29-34
sa0db2ODNmo.one_line: The closing verses of Luqman: Allah the All-Aware of intentions, patience and gratitude, and a Day when no parent avails a child.
sa0db2ODNmo.summary: Finishing Surat Luqman, he reads the closing page as Allah's commentary on Luqman's counsel. Healthy relations between generations need balance: neither the blind obedience of the old Arabs nor outright disobedience. The verses on night entering day and the sun and moon running to a set term are addressed to each individual: nothing lasts, young or old. Allah is al-Khabir, aware of the intentions behind deeds, and since no law can fix a corrupt intention, only fear of al-Haqq, al-Aliyy al-Kabir can. The ship image shows the two states of the believer, patience and gratitude, with gratitude the base and patience its placeholder, against the faithless ingrate who forgets his rescue. The call to all mankind to fear a Day when no parent avails a child and no child avails a parent means each is responsible for himself and serves the other only to save himself, and that neither generation replaces the other. Every generation repeats the same complaints about the next, but the Prophet never belittled the young and promoted them. The five keys of the unseen remind all that no one knows everything, so each should offer advice humbly, as Luqman did.

outline.heading: Recap: the pages that comment on Luqman's story
outline.gist: As in Al-Kahf, a central story is followed by verses that comment on it and draw attention to what we might have missed.

outline.heading: Balance between blind obedience and disobedience
outline.gist: The Quran did not come to reinforce ancestor worship but to correct it: benefit from elders, keep company with them kindly, and stay independent in belief.

outline.heading: Each generation acts for Allah, not as repayment
outline.gist: Elders raise and the young honour for Allah's sake, not as a transaction.

outline.heading: The Arabs who wanted sons for their own strength
outline.gist: Having children to gain protection and status led to despising daughters, the root of a chain of evils.

outline.heading: The pivotal verse: the firmest handhold
outline.gist: Submitting one's face to Allah alone, with ihsan, is the axis of these two pages and improves every relationship.

outline.heading: Recitation, and a note on two consecutive ha's
outline.gist: Reads verses 29 and 30 and notes that the two ha's are pronounced separately in this reading.

outline.heading: 'Do you not see' in the singular: an address to each person
outline.gist: Contrasted with the plural in verse 20, which called society to shared gratitude, this verse addresses each individual.

outline.heading: Night into day: nothing lasts
outline.gist: Whether old or young, do not deceive yourself that you are permanent.

outline.heading: Sun and moon to an appointed term; time itself ends
outline.gist: We understand time through day and night; prisoners deprived of them lose their minds; even this motion has a set end.

outline.heading: Al-Khabir: knowing what is in the chest
outline.gist: Distinguishes al-Alim, al-Sami, al-Basir, al-Latif and al-Khabir; al-Khabir knows intentions that leave no trace in the world of the senses.

outline.heading: No law can fix a corrupt intention
outline.gist: People can harm others without ever breaking a law; only Allah's knowledge of intentions reaches this, and He brings it out on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Allah is al-Haqq; what they call on besides Him is falsehood
outline.gist: Truth precedes justice; every word and act will be weighed on the scale of truth, and anything done for other than Him is void.

outline.heading: Relationships cannot be governed by rules alone
outline.gist: Institutions and laws can set conditions, but in marriage or any relationship a person with bad intention will find a way around them.

outline.heading: Al-Aliyy al-Kabir: names of majesty and warning
outline.gist: These names are used to warn; the human stands in awe before the One who is Truth and above all.

outline.heading: Recitation of the ship verses
outline.gist: Reads verses 31 and 32.

outline.heading: Two states: patience and gratitude
outline.gist: Gratitude is the default state; patience is the temporary substitute that keeps one under the umbrella of gratitude when harm makes thanks impossible.

outline.heading: Ships run by Allah's favour; waves like canopies
outline.gist: Had wood not floated humanity would never have spread; waves tower like mountains, as the mountain was raised over the Children of Israel.

outline.heading: Sincere in the storm
outline.gist: In terror, as when a plane drops, people repent and purify their intentions instantly; confess before death while it still helps.

outline.heading: 'Some of them are moderate': the promise half kept
outline.gist: Rescued, some trim their great sincerity, like one who vowed all his wealth and gave a little; look at yourself, not at those who forgot your favours.

outline.heading: Khattar and kafur: the opposite of sabbar and shakur
outline.gist: Khattar lacks patience and kafur lacks gratitude; kufr in its basic sense is the opposite of gratitude; ships, like having children, are a blessing with real risk.

outline.heading: Khattar: losing one's composure
outline.gist: The word appears only here: one who in hardship collapses and humiliates himself instead of holding firm.

outline.heading: Recitation of the closing verses
outline.gist: Reads verses 33 and 34.

outline.heading: 'O mankind, fear your Lord': the page as preparation
outline.gist: Addressed to all people because the generational problem exists in every society; the whole page introduced who your Lord is before commanding taqwa.

outline.heading: No parent avails a child, no child a parent
outline.gist: No one can step in for another on that Day; intercession happens only with Allah's permission.

outline.heading: Nuh and his son; righteous offspring joined to parents
outline.gist: Nuh's plea was refused because his son was not righteous, while believing descendants are raised to their parents' rank.

outline.heading: The Prophet tells his family to save themselves
outline.gist: Each is responsible for himself and does good to the other to save himself; the nominal sentence stresses that the child can never avail the parent.

outline.heading: Neither generation substitutes for the other
outline.gist: A second meaning of yajzi: one generation does not replace the other; every generation repeats the same tired complaints about the next.

outline.heading: The Prophet never belittled the young
outline.gist: He excused, forgave and promoted the young into leadership; deceptive worldly life and Shaytan make people think otherwise.

outline.heading: The five keys of the unseen: no one knows everything
outline.gist: Conflict is over who knows more; only Allah knows the Hour, the rain, the womb, tomorrow and where one dies, so all should be humble.

outline.heading: Back to Luqman's gentle counsel
outline.gist: Luqman advised with love and even humour, without wanting control over his son.

outline.heading: Reread Luqman after the commentary
outline.gist: Returning to Luqman's words after Allah's commentary reveals more depth.

outline.heading: Outro

Xx3t5lMYJl8.speaker_note: Continues his own Al-Qiyamah tafseer from the previous week and speaks of counselling people at his centre.
Xx3t5lMYJl8.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Qiyamah, Part 2: Verses 7-19
Xx3t5lMYJl8.one_line: Scenes of the Day with nowhere to flee, and the core of the passage: every human has full insight into himself and should stop self-deception.
Xx3t5lMYJl8.summary: The sheikh explains why Al-Qiyamah addresses the mind before the heart: emotions are the most valuable and vulnerable part of a person, so reason must clear the ground before the heart is invested, in faith as in marriage. After recapping the oaths, he moves through the scenes of the Day: eyes stunned as if by lightning, the moon eclipsed, sun and moon brought together, and man asking where to flee. Unlike any earthly disaster, there is no shelter and no cover; every road ends before Allah, the final residence. Man is told what he sent ahead and what he held back, yet verses 14 and 15 reach the heart of the passage: the human being is insight upon himself, even when he offers excuses. Children lie when no one can prove otherwise, adults perfect the habit, and some will even swear falsely to Allah. He urges honesty with others, and at the very least with oneself, citing the man whose ninety-nine scrolls of sin were outweighed by one card because he argued nothing. He reads verses 16-19 two ways: as guidance to the Prophet on receiving revelation, or as words to a person hurrying past the shameful parts of his own book. When people deny, their own limbs testify, so tap into that insight now.

outline.heading: A surah that speaks to the intellect
outline.gist: He takes Al-Qiyamah slowly because its dawah challenges logic and purpose rather than greed or fear, unlike the two surahs that follow it.

outline.heading: Move greed and fear one step past death
outline.gist: Humans are naturally greedy and scared of the future; no one is faulted for that, as long as both emotions reach beyond this life.

outline.heading: The mind governs the heart
outline.gist: Following the heart blindly almost always ends in regret. The deen stimulates the intellect first, then invests the heart fully; emotions built on a lie collapse violently.

outline.heading: Your heart is what you have of most value
outline.gist: Money is the cheapest thing you can give, time is worth more, and your love and passion are the most valuable and vulnerable. Opening it to everyone without thought sets you up for scars.

outline.heading: Marriage paves the ground for the heart
outline.gist: Marriage makes sure the right questions are asked, often by experienced people, before you fall in love. Islam is where your heart belongs fully, but make sure the reasoning is right first.

outline.heading: Withdrawn love does not return the same
outline.gist: Pulling back love leaves the heart hesitant and weaker, so reason comes first; the surah's first oath is by the conscience that questions every choice.

outline.heading: Recitation from verse seven
outline.gist: He recites to the end of the page, promising to read it all with translation later.

outline.heading: Stopping on a doubled letter
outline.gist: A tajweed note: stopping on a letter with shaddah requires emphasizing it; such verse endings are rare in the Quran.

outline.heading: Recap: the two oaths and man's excuse
outline.gist: Allah swears by the Day He takes a stand on each person and by the conscience that knows the right answer whatever Google says. Man's real problem is wanting a guilt-free life of sin.

outline.heading: When is this Day? Is there time?
outline.gist: Wanting to sin, man asks when the Day will be, hoping he still has time to do his thing.

outline.heading: Eyes stunned as if by lightning
outline.gist: Many Quranic scenes describe the onlooker rather than the event. Bariqa comes from lightning: eyes fixed and dilated by a sight never seen before.

outline.heading: The moon eclipsed, sun and moon joined
outline.gist: Khusuf is the dimming of the moon; the cosmos collapses in on itself and the sun crashes into the moon.

outline.heading: Looking for a safe place in a disaster
outline.gist: In tornadoes, earthquakes or fires we want to gather our family, drive away and find shelter, even an underground bunker.

outline.heading: Nowhere to run when the universe collapses
outline.gist: Mountains crumble, valleys fill and seas burn, and everyone is driven to one place, exposed. Man asks where the escape is.

outline.heading: No refuge, no cover
outline.gist: Allah Himself answers: no wazar. The root means a cover, which is why sin (wizr) is so called, as it covers the heart and good deeds.

outline.heading: Al-mustaqarr: the final residence
outline.gist: Everything in this world is temporary. The only place to run to is your Lord, where you settle for good.

outline.heading: All roads lead back to Allah
outline.gist: Whatever path you take, you are marching toward Him and will find yourself standing before Him.

outline.heading: The surah that speaks to every insan
outline.gist: No surah uses the word insan as often, even the long ones; the experience is universal regardless of race, religion, age or sex.

outline.heading: Informed of what he sent ahead and held back
outline.gist: Man is told what moved him closer to Allah and what pulled him back, or what he did early and late in life. A hadith qudsi: it is only your deeds that I count for you.

outline.heading: Our existence is that simple
outline.gist: A few laps around the sun and we are gone; one meteor erases every trace. We over-complicate it: you return to Allah, the good and bad are shown and added up.

outline.heading: Another bal: the real problem
outline.gist: There is nowhere to run. Every bal in the surah signals that what came before is not the real issue.

outline.heading: Basirah: insight, not eyesight
outline.gist: The real issue is that man has full insight into his intentions, emotions and choices. It is not the eyes that go blind but the hearts in the chests.

outline.heading: Man is insight upon himself
outline.gist: First doubt about the bones, then the wish for guilt-free sin, and finally the truth: he is insight upon himself, yet lies to himself and others to avoid changing.

outline.heading: We hate being told we were the problem
outline.gist: We avoid answers that demand different choices and find it painful to hear that we caused a failure.

outline.heading: A generation that cannot take feedback
outline.gist: Criticism now comes sandwiched, and people collapse into years of therapy when told plainly they did it wrong; he wonders how we will survive that.

outline.heading: Children lie when no one can prove it
outline.gist: A child who was not seen defends a false story because his parents cannot prove otherwise, equating unprovable with untrue.

outline.heading: Your parents know because they were you
outline.gist: Parents know the real motive because they once did the same thing, though they will not admit it.

outline.heading: Adults perfect the habit
outline.gist: Left unchecked, the habit grows until nothing is admitted unless caught red-handed, and even then the narrative is shaped to look less malicious.

outline.heading: Swearing falsely to Allah
outline.gist: Some will swear to Allah on that Day as they swear to people, having lied so long they no longer know what is true.

outline.heading: The good news: you have insight
outline.gist: You can see your faults, accept blame and improve. Some people come to him with no insight at all, ignoring their share of the blame.

outline.heading: Hearing the holes in their story
outline.gist: When someone cannot see the blame their own account reveals, he ends the meeting, because they have chosen to lie to themselves.

outline.heading: Even if he offers his excuses
outline.gist: People cannot see through you, but Allah will lay everything open, however many excuses about being tired or overworked are thrown out.

outline.heading: At least admit it to yourself
outline.gist: If you cannot admit fault to others, say it to yourself: my intention was bad, I was negligent, I knew what I was doing.

outline.heading: Blankets over the radio
outline.gist: Self-deception is smothering a radio that keeps telling you the truth. He is not licensing lying to people; honesty with all is best, but never fail to be honest with yourself.

outline.heading: Deep inside you know He is there
outline.gist: Whatever an atheist argues, insight tells you that you were never alone, that He gave you much and expects something, and that responsibility means change.

outline.heading: Not lying to Allah will save you
outline.gist: However many mistakes and lies to others, keeping that inner honesty brings the humility that will serve you when you come to Him.

outline.heading: The man with ninety-nine scrolls
outline.gist: A man's sins tower on his scale like the Burj Khalifa. Asked whether the recording angels wronged him or he has an excuse, he says no: that was me.

outline.heading: The card that outweighs everything
outline.gist: Called back with the match seemingly lost, he is given a card bearing the testimony of faith; it sends the scrolls flying, for nothing outweighs Allah's name.

outline.heading: They argued nothing
outline.gist: The killer of many and others in the sunnah who were forgiven share one trait: they sat quietly and admitted everything.

outline.heading: I have nothing to say but Your mercy
outline.gist: We all sin, but meeting Allah ashamed, with nothing to defend yourself with after His blessings, is powerful; the alternative is a cooked narrative of parents, school and hardship.

outline.heading: Excuses beat tired parents, not Allah
outline.gist: A child with fifty excuses outlasts a tired mother or a father home after ten hours of work; that skill will not work with Allah.

outline.heading: Advice to the young: do not master self-deception
outline.gist: As an older brother he urges young people to strengthen their conscience and insight, accept accountability for each mistake and grow into better adults. He recites the last verses.

outline.heading: First reading: the Prophet and revelation
outline.gist: A common view takes verses 16-19 as an aside to the Prophet: do not rush your tongue to memorize; Allah will gather, recite and explain it. He accepts it as correct.

outline.heading: Second reading: the one reading his own book
outline.gist: He prefers the view that fits the flow: on the Day a person reading his record hurries past the embarrassing parts and is told not to rush.

outline.heading: Slow down: We will explain why you did it
outline.gist: Allah compiled the book and will have it recited slowly, then clarify every act and its motive; you speed because you know the fault is yours.

outline.heading: Repent while defence is still possible
outline.gist: In this world you found a way around your faults; there, nothing defends you. Acknowledge and repent now and Allah will forgive.

outline.heading: Your own limbs will testify
outline.gist: Those who have shut down their insight will deny, so Allah makes their tongues, hands, feet and skin speak against them.

outline.heading: Tap into your insight
outline.gist: The surah's dawah speaks to the part of you that knows the truth and that He is there. Use it instead of fighting or fleeing it, and live with more peace.

ZydqE-N_xZA.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Mortality, Episode 22
ZydqE-N_xZA.one_line: Opening the pillar of accepting mortality and accountability: why nothing in the deen works without it, Adam's fear of death, and how to accept it.
ZydqE-N_xZA.summary: The sheikh begins the second of his five pillars of tazkiyah: accepting mortality and accountability to Allah. He warns it is the topic that thins the crowd, yet without it the whole ethical argument of Islam collapses, since being good only makes sense to the privileged unless there is death and judgment. A third of the Quran deals with it, and the companions were so convinced that the Prophet had to restrain them. He separates death, an unknown moment not worth obsessing over and never to be celebrated, from mortality, the fact that you will end, which must be accepted and not merely known. Adam had everything, yet Shaytan reached him only through the fear of death, offering the tree of immortality; that fear drove the first act of disobedience. Adam later gave Dawud forty of his years and nearly asked for them back. Imagining immortality shows that time would lose all value. Earlier generations met death often; modern people meet it late and exempt themselves, as drivers do from traffic rules. He asks listeners to contemplate their mortality carefully, with a mental-health caution, and points to the calm deaths of the Prophet, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Bilal, his oncology patients, and the hadith on weakness from fear of death.

outline.heading: Opening
The five pillars of tazkiyah
outline.gist: Self-value, accepting mortality and accountability, self-honesty, sensitivity and etiquette, and moral frugality or wara'.

outline.heading: The crowd thinner
outline.gist: People lose interest when mortality comes up, yet every principle and ethic of the deen crumbles without it.

outline.heading: Accountability versus self-accountability
outline.gist: Muhasabah is questioning yourself; accepting accountability is accepting that Allah will question you.

outline.heading: The companions needed restraining
outline.gist: The Prophet's task was to pull them back from excess, because the hereafter was crystal clear to them.

outline.heading: A third of the Quran
outline.gist: Almost every surah speaks of the hereafter, reachable only through death.

outline.heading: Ethics without accountability only persuade the privileged
outline.gist: Being good is easy to argue when a system benefits you; for those on the losing side, morality without judgment has no basis.

outline.heading: The Arabs accepted death but denied accountability
outline.gist: They knew Allah and knew they would die; what they rejected was resurrection and the reckoning it brings.

outline.heading: His third attempt at this topic
outline.gist: Twice he began tazkiyah here and stopped; there is no point changing the nafs without accepting these two facts.

outline.heading: Remove them and see what stands
outline.gist: Take mortality, then accountability, out of the deen and no argument survives.

outline.heading: Death is a moment; do not obsess over it
outline.gist: Death is an unknown point in time that will always come too early; planning for or fearing that moment is pointless.

outline.heading: We never celebrate death; we accept mortality
outline.gist: Even a martyr's death is a calamity; what must be accepted is that you will end.

outline.heading: Knowing is not accepting
outline.gist: Knowing you will die differs greatly from accepting it, which the coming weeks will show.

outline.heading: Adam had everything
outline.gist: Companionship, safety, food, beauty and closeness to Allah, with one tree forbidden.

outline.heading: The tree of immortality
outline.gist: It was not curiosity about the forbidden; Shaytan offered him eternal life.

outline.heading: The deal of life ends in death
outline.gist: Like a young adult told the whole plan of life, Adam liked everything except that he was a servant and would die.

outline.heading: Fear of death caused the first sin
outline.gist: Shaytan tried pitch after pitch until immortality made Adam flinch, then swore he was a sincere adviser.

outline.heading: A lifetime learning to accept
outline.gist: Adam spent the rest of his life accepting mortality; Allah showed him his descendants as points of light.

outline.heading: Adam's only question about Dawud
outline.gist: He asked only how long Dawud would live, as parents ache knowing their children will die.

outline.heading: Forty years given and almost taken back
outline.gist: When the angel came, Adam nearly asked for the years back; life's basic beauty makes losing it hard.

outline.heading: If you lived forever, time would be worthless
outline.gist: Time is the one capital you can never buy back; without an end, nothing would ever be done today.

outline.heading: Accept it, do not celebrate it
outline.gist: Not enjoying or welcoming mortality, but being at peace that it can come at any moment, which takes steps.

outline.heading: Earlier generations lived alongside death
outline.gist: With a median lifespan around 38, war and no antibiotics, the companions saw death often; modern medicine made it a stranger.

outline.heading: Death is enough as a reminder
outline.gist: Remembering death needed little prompting in their time, so the Prophet's advice was simply to remember it.

outline.heading: We meet death late in life
outline.gist: In the West most people have no experience of death until late and are never taught about it when young.

outline.heading: The human gift of self-exemption
outline.gist: Rules apply to everyone but slightly less to me, as on the road or in a queue; we do the same with death.

outline.heading: Contemplate your own mortality
outline.gist: This week, think about what your end would look and feel like.

outline.heading: A caution for those who are struggling
outline.gist: Anyone struggling with mental health or a reason to live should be careful and discuss this with their therapist.

outline.heading: Near-death experiences wear off
outline.gist: People change after a brush with death, then slide back within years because mortality was never truly accepted.

outline.heading: A good ending is what counts
outline.gist: The Prophet kept asking for a good end; marriages and tournaments are remembered by how they end.

outline.heading: How the Prophet and companions died
outline.gist: The Prophet chose the highest companion; Abu Bakr corrected Aisha's poetry, Umar asked for his face on the ground, Uthman refused bloodshed, Bilal smiled to meet his loved ones.

outline.heading: Death is hard for everyone
outline.gist: The stupor of death comes to all; preparation changes how it is met.

outline.heading: Conversations about mortality in oncology
outline.gist: Many of his clinic visits are, in effect, conversations about death coming sooner than hoped, and people respond according to how they lived.

outline.heading: The dying scholar and his grandsons
outline.gist: Prompted to say la ilaha illa Allah, he told them it was mixed in his blood and to go learn it themselves.

outline.heading: The 92-year-old who wanted two more years
outline.gist: Asked what he hoped for, a gravely ill patient wanted two more years, and then two more: death is never far enough away.

outline.heading: A different way to live
outline.gist: Accepting mortality and accountability gave the companions a different view of life, as near-death survivors sometimes gain.

outline.heading: Non-believers who die calmer than Muslims
outline.gist: He has seen people without faith meet death calmly; a Muslim cannot afford to leave mortality unaccepted.

outline.heading: Weakness from fear of death
outline.gist: The Prophet foretold a numerous but weak ummah crippled by love of the world and dislike of death; fear drove Adam's only mistake.

outline.heading: Outro

16:90.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِ وَٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنِ وَإِيتَآيِٕ ذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَيَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَٱلۡبَغۡيِۚ يَعِظُكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
16:90.en: Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded

16:91.en: And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, [O believers], and do not break oaths after their confirmation while you have made Allah, over you, a witness. Indeed, Allah knows what you do

16:92.ar: وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّتِي نَقَضَتۡ غَزۡلَهَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنكَٰثࣰ ا تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيۡمَٰنَكُمۡ دَخَلَۢا بَيۡنَكُمۡ أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرۡبَىٰ مِنۡ أُمَّةٍۚ إِنَّمَا يَبۡلُوكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦۚ وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ لَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَا كُنتُمۡ فِيهِ تَخۡتَلِفُونَ
16:92.en: And do not be like she who untwisted her spun thread after it was strong [by] taking your oaths as [means of] deceit between you because one community is more plentiful [in number or wealth] than another community. 16:93.ar: وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ وَلَٰكِن يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَلَتُسۡـَٔلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
16:93.en: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you [of] one religion, but He causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do

cdxrMr7YQzk.title: Listening to the Divine: An-Nahl 90-97, Part 2
cdxrMr7YQzk.one_line: Finishing An-Nahl 90-97: the verse that settled Uthman ibn Maz'un's faith, the covenant that is not for sale, promised trials, and the good life.
cdxrMr7YQzk.summary: Part two of his khutbah on An-Nahl 90-97, finishing the commentary he could not complete the week before. He first shows the weight of 16:90, the verse every khutbah closes with: Imam Ahmad records that Uthman ibn Maz'un, a wealthy Qurayshi who had accepted Islam only out of shyness before the Prophet, said faith settled in his heart when he heard it, and when the Prophet offered himself to twenty-six tribes in ten days, Mafruq of Banu Shayban recognized in it a call to noble character. The verses then turn to the covenant: do not make or unravel commitments out of self-interest, fear or siding with the stronger party, because everything you have runs out; a man who sold his principles enjoys the gain for forty years and regrets it in his seventies with the grave in view. Everyone has a price, so is your covenant with Allah for sale? Even supreme leadership of the planet would leave you cheap. The Quran promises the individual nothing in this world except trials and does not soften that to market itself. Its single worldly promise is the good life of 16:97, which the Arabic second khutbah locates not in wealth, status or health but in a tranquil heart with a purpose beyond its instincts.

outline.heading: Opening
He commands and He forbids
outline.gist: Allah opens by stating that He commands certain things and prohibits others; that emphasis is why these verses are always recited in khutbahs, and accepting them is entering a covenant.

outline.heading: Uthman ibn Maz'un: the verse that settled his faith
outline.gist: Imam Ahmad's narration: a wealthy Qurayshi who admired the Prophet's selflessness accepted Islam out of shyness, unsure of it, until these verses were recited and faith settled in his heart.

outline.heading: Twenty-six tribes in ten days
outline.gist: In the tenth year of prophethood the Prophet presented himself to tribe after tribe, exhausting days of refusals and insults, until Banu Shayban gave a reasonable hearing and their leader Mafruq ibn Amr asked what he was calling to.

outline.heading: Mafruq: you call to noble character
outline.gist: On hearing 16:90 Mafruq said he was calling to noble character and good deeds and that those who denied him had wronged themselves, though his tribe could not offer protection.

outline.heading: Listen to Allah directly
outline.gist: Spend less time listening to people like him; Allah is addressing you as an individual. The imam's only function is to help you understand the Book, and imams carry no other status.

outline.heading: Covenants made from interest or fear
outline.gist: After the commands and prohibitions comes the covenant: do not be like the woman who unravelled her yarn, and do not make or break covenants for personal benefit, to be on the stronger side, or out of fear or greed.

outline.heading: All you have is finite
outline.gist: Do not use oaths as a means of corruption, because everything in this world runs out: you enjoy the gain in your thirties, forties and fifties, then sickness comes and nothing matters.

outline.heading: Regret at seventy
outline.gist: Old and tired, with the grave beyond the horizon, you regret forty years of standing by what you knew was wrong because a tribe, country or way of life was popular or profitable, and you can no longer enjoy what you gained.

outline.heading: Is your covenant for sale?
outline.gist: Hold to justice, excellence and the rest to the end. Someday someone will put a price on your word and loyalty; everyone is for sale at the right price. Even supreme leadership of the earth would make you cheap and the covenant cheaply sold.

outline.heading: Selling out subtly: selective justice
outline.gist: Selling the covenant can mean being fair only to people you like and not to a group that looks, smells or speaks differently; and whatever you gain runs out.

outline.heading: Promised nothing but trials
outline.gist: The individual is promised nothing in this world. Did people think they would say 'we believe' and not be tested? Allah tests to make known who was truthful and who lied.

outline.heading: Trials are part of the covenant
outline.gist: Trials are promised, not a possibility: whoever believes should prepare for tribulation, and the most tested are the prophets, then the righteous, then the next best.

outline.heading: Allah does not need to market His teachings
outline.gist: From a marketing standpoint promising trials is a poor pitch, but there is no lying in this story; Allah does not soften the consequences. Accept the covenant and stand by it.

outline.heading: Hayat tayyibah: the ripe fruit
outline.gist: Whoever does good as a believer, male or female, receives a good life. Tayyib describes ripe fruit, full of water and sweetness, where unripe fruit is empty and sour.

outline.heading: A life with purpose beyond instinct
outline.gist: The good life is fulfilment: a life that meant something beyond basic needs and urges, aimed at a goal Allah beautified, that you look back on at peace and can sleep on each night, rich or poor, healthy or sick, long or short.

outline.heading: The more you get, the more you need
outline.gist: Every human seeks fulfilment whether they know it or not; the young do not see it yet, but later they eat, travel and gather a great deal and are never filled by it.

outline.heading: Interlude
The one worldly promise to the individual
outline.gist: Every Quranic promise to believers concerns the Hereafter; the ummah is promised establishment on earth, but the individual only repeated trials and the command to be patient, except for this verse. It does not promise long life, health or power.

outline.heading: The good life lives in the heart
outline.gist: We ask Allah for wealth, health and status but are not promised them; the intelligent person knows quality of life lies in a tranquil heart filled with closeness to its Lord that knows its purpose.

outline.heading: Sheikh, I am tired
outline.gist: Living for something higher than oneself is what humans have sought since creation; the man whose wealth, travel, food, friends and children multiply yet feels empty is seeking tranquility in the wrong place. Fulfil the covenant: justice, excellence, giving to kin.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.note: The covenant with Allah must be kept to the end; commitments made or unravelled for self-interest, fear or the stronger side are corruption, and no price, not even rule of the planet, justifies selling it.

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: Everyone is for sale at the right price, so he asks whether you are; standing by what you know is wrong because it is popular or profitable ends in regret when you can no longer enjoy the gain.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: The good life promised in 16:97 is fulfilment: a life that meant something beyond needs and instincts, directed to a goal Allah beautified, which is what every human seeks whether they know it yet or not.

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: Quality of life is not in wealth, status, kingdom or health but in a tranquil heart close to its Lord; the man who has everything and is tired is searching in the wrong place.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: The individual is promised nothing in this world except trials, which separate the truthful from the liars; the prophets were tested hardest, and Allah does not soften this to make the message easier to sell.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: 16:90 is a compact statement of Islam's commands and prohibitions, so weighty that it settled Uthman ibn Maz'un's faith and made Mafruq recognize a call to noble character.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Uthman ibn Maz'un's conversion out of shyness, and the exhausting tour of twenty-six tribes in ten days in the tenth year that produced one reasonable hearing from Banu Shayban.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: Uthman ibn Maz'un: a wealthy man who admired the Prophet's selflessness before he believed, and whose faith became certain through the Quran.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: What you have runs out: wealth and status are enjoyed for a few decades, then sickness and age remove the capacity to enjoy them while the regret remains.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Eating, drinking, travelling and acquiring a lot never fills the inner need; the more you get the more you need.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Selling the covenant includes being just only to people you like and withholding fairness from a group that looks, smells or speaks differently.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Listen to Allah speaking to you directly; the imam's whole job is to help you understand the Book, and once you understand it yourself you need nothing from him.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: In your seventies, tired and sick, you see the grave beyond the horizon and can no longer enjoy what you compromised your principles for.

quran.point: Did people think they would be left alone saying 'we believe' without being tested? Allah tests to make known the truthful and the liars.

hadith.gist: The Prophet recited An-Nahl 90-91 to Uthman ibn Maz'un, who said that was the moment faith settled in his heart; he had accepted Islam earlier only out of shyness before the Prophet.

Allah commanded the Prophet to present himself to the tribes; he went to Banu Shayban, and when their leader Mafruq ibn Amr asked what he called to, he recited 16:90, and Mafruq said he was calling to noble character and good deeds and that those who denied him had wronged themselves.
Whoever believes in Allah should prepare himself to be clothed in tribulation.
The most severely tested people are the prophets, then the righteous, then the next best and the next best.

Everyone is for sale at the right price; are you?
Is your covenant with Allah for sale?
Allah does not need to market His teachings
You are promised nothing as an individual except trials
You are looking for tranquility in the wrong place

stories.who: Uthman ibn Maz'un
stories.point: A wealthy Qurayshi unmoved by the message but drawn by the Prophet's selflessness accepted Islam out of shyness; only An-Nahl 90 settled faith in his heart, showing the verse's power.

stories.who: Mafruq ibn Amr and Banu Shayban
stories.point: After twenty-six tribes in ten days rejected or insulted him, the Prophet found one reasonable hearing; Mafruq recognized 16:90 as a call to noble character even though his tribe could not protect him.

stories.who: The man who sold his principles and regrets them at seventy
stories.point: He sided with the popular or profitable choice he knew was wrong, enjoyed it for decades, and ended sick and tired with the grave in view and nothing but regret.

stories.who: The man who has everything and tells the sheikh he is tired
stories.point: Wealth, travel, food, friends and children multiplied and he is still empty, because tranquility was sought in the wrong place; the good life comes from fulfilling the covenant.

contemporary: Compromising principles to side with the popular tribe, country or way of life, or because someone offers a price for your loyalty
Selective justice: being fair only to people you like and not to a group that looks, smells or speaks differently
A marketing-style objection that promising trials is a poor way to sell a message
Affluent lives full of food, travel, friends and children that still feel empty ('Sheikh, I am tired')
takeaways: Listen to Allah directly in these verses; use the imam only to understand them better
Keep your covenant with Allah to the end, and never make or break commitments out of self-interest, fear or siding with the stronger party
Refuse any price for your principles, since every gain runs out while what is with Allah remains, and extend justice even to people you dislike
Expect trials as part of the covenant rather than a sign that something has gone wrong
Seek the good life where it actually lies: a tranquil heart close to Allah with a purpose beyond your instincts, not in wealth, status or health

16:90.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡمُرُ بِٱلۡعَدۡلِ وَٱلۡإِحۡسَٰنِ وَإِيتَآيِٕ ذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَيَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَٱلۡبَغۡيِۚ يَعِظُكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
16:90.en: Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded

16:91.ar: وَأَوۡفُواْ بِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا عَٰهَدتُّمۡ وَلَا تَنقُضُواْ ٱلۡأَيۡمَٰنَ بَعۡدَ تَوۡكِيدِهَا وَقَدۡ جَعَلۡتُمُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ كَفِيلًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
16:91.en: And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, [O believers], and do not break oaths after their confirmation while you have made Allah, over you, a witness. Indeed, Allah knows what you do

16:92.ar: وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّتِي نَقَضَتۡ غَزۡلَهَا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنكَٰثࣰ ا تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيۡمَٰنَكُمۡ دَخَلَۢا بَيۡنَكُمۡ أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرۡبَىٰ مِنۡ أُمَّةٍۚ إِنَّمَا يَبۡلُوكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦۚ وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ لَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَا كُنتُمۡ فِيهِ تَخۡتَلِفُونَ
16:92.en: And do not be like she who untwisted her spun thread after it was strong [by] taking your oaths as [means of] deceit between you because one community is more plentiful [in number or wealth] than another community. Allah only tries you thereby. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ

16:93.ar: وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ وَلَٰكِن يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَلَتُسۡـَٔلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
16:93.en: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you [of] one religion, but He causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do

16:94.ar: وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَكُمۡ دَخَلَۢا بَيۡنَكُمۡ فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمُۢ بَعۡدَ ثُبُوتِهَا وَتَذُوقُواْ ٱلسُّوٓءَ بِمَا صَدَدتُّمۡ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَكُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
16:94.en: And do not take your oaths as [means of] deceit between you, lest a foot slip after it was [once] firm, and you would taste evil [in this world] for what [people] you diverted from the way of Allah, and you would have [in the Hereafter] a great punishment

16:95.ar: وَلَا تَشۡتَرُواْ بِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ ثَمَنࣰ ا قَلِيلًاۚ إِنَّمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
16:95.en: And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is best for you, if only you could know

16:96.ar: مَا عِندَكُمۡ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقࣲۗ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوٓاْ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:96.en: Whatever you have will end, but what Allah has is lasting. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do

16:97.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَلَنُحۡيِيَنَّهُۥ حَيَوٰةࣰ طَيِّبَةࣰۖ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّهُمۡ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:97.en: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do

aEi34jg4Ic8.speaker: adnan
aEi34jg4Ic8.speaker_note: Speaks of 'how I have been giving my khutbahs over the last years' and launches his own new series; single voice throughout after the Arabic opening.
aEi34jg4Ic8.title: Listening to the Divine: Al-Nahl 90-97
aEi34jg4Ic8.one_line: Launches a recite-and-translate khutbah series with An-Nahl 90-97 on justice and keeping covenants, prefaced by a call to respond to Sudan as to Gaza.
aEi34jg4Ic8.summary: He opens with a preface that has nothing to do with the series: the community mobilized for Gaza, so it must mobilize the same way for Sudan. He names a long-standing problem in the ummah, favoritism in whose suffering gets attention, and says Muslims from Africa, South Asia and China have accepted that nobody cares about them. The older generation has normalized ignoring certain crises; the children must learn to respond equally. He then introduces a new format: like the Prophet sometimes did, he will simply recite a passage, translate it slowly and explain it, because Muslims raised with the Quran have habituated listening without processing. The passage is An-Nahl 90-97, the verses that for some 1200 years have closed every Friday khutbah by a caliph's decree, and the verses that made Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah admit this was not human speech before Abu Jahl pressured him into calling it magic. He walks through them: three commands and three prohibitions, fulfilling the covenant, not unspinning the yarn, not treating oaths as instruments of personal interest, the foot that slips after standing firm, not selling Allah's covenant cheaply because what you hold runs out while what is with Allah remains, and the good life promised to the believer who does good.

outline.heading: Opening
Respond to Sudan as you did to Gaza
outline.gist: Before the series: the community answered the genocide in Gaza with real will to change, and it owes the same response to the crisis in Sudan. Sudan is the measure of a wider problem: favoritism in whose pain counts.

outline.heading: An ummah that ranks pain has no future
outline.gist: He grew up questioning why one Muslim crisis drew a response and a similar one elsewhere did not; any human crisis deserves a response, and an ummah that ranks its members' suffering cannot succeed.

outline.heading: Ask the forgotten
outline.gist: Muslims from parts of Africa, South Asia, China or Europe will say they have endured systematic oppression for decades, even a century, and have made peace with the idea that no fellow Muslim cares.

outline.heading: Feel for them as for your own
outline.gist: People in Sudan face circumstances you would never accept for yourself or a loved one; if that is how you feel about those close to you, you must feel it for those who are different.

outline.heading: Our children must respond equally
outline.gist: The older generation got used to responding to some regions and ignoring others; the children must react to a Muslim suffering in Afghanistan, Myanmar or China as they would to one in Sudan, Somalia, Syria, Iraq or Palestine.

outline.heading: Normalized struggles and the Gaza benchmark
outline.gist: People feel left out because some struggles were normalized and ignored. The advocacy, signs and giving shown for Gaza must be the same everywhere; they are not less. Dua for Sudan, Yemen, Afghanistan and the forgotten.

outline.heading: The Prophet's khutbahs of pure recitation
outline.gist: The Prophet would often stand on the minbar and give a khutbah that was only Quran: after his introduction he recited Surah Qaf in full by some narrations, or particular passages by others.

outline.heading: A weekly reminder of what the Divine expects
outline.gist: The point of the Friday gathering is that someone reminds the community of the Divine's teachings and the direction He wants; nothing does that better than listening to Him directly.

outline.heading: Habituated listening
outline.gist: Many raised with the Quran have learned to hear it without processing it the way they process ordinary speech; he has heard this for years from people, so the coming khutbahs will each take one passage.

outline.heading: The verse that closes every khutbah
outline.gist: He will recite slowly, then translate and explain, so people learn to listen. These verses are usually heard at the end of khutbahs because a caliph decreed that 16:90 replace something else said there, a practice of some 1200 years.

outline.heading: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah: not the speech of a human
outline.gist: Hearing these verses, al-Walid swore they were not human speech, fruitful above and abundant below, rising and never surpassed; under Abu Jahl's pressure he called them inherited magic.

outline.heading: Recitation of the passage
outline.gist: He recites An-Nahl 90 to 97 in full, slowly.

outline.heading: Justice, excellence and giving to kin; indecency, evil and oppression
outline.gist: Allah commands justice, ihsan and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing and oppression, admonishing so that you remember: three things you must do and three you must not.

outline.heading: Accepting the covenant
outline.gist: If you put out your hand and accept these terms, you have taken a covenant with Allah; do not break oaths after confirming them, having made Allah your guarantor, for He knows what you do.

outline.heading: The woman who unspun her yarn
outline.gist: An Arabian proverb: a woman who lost her mind spun firm yarn into strong fabric and then unspun it all. Do not build something firm and useful and then undo it yourself.

outline.heading: Oaths as instruments of interest
outline.gist: Taking oaths as deceit so that one group may be greater than another means entering a covenant corruptly, for personal interest rather than truth and righteousness.

outline.heading: May your word stand for something
outline.gist: Do not cherry-pick commitments by who is stronger or more useful to you; be a person of principle who stands by an oath because it is correct and just. Allah tests you by it.

outline.heading: Not forced into one nation
outline.gist: Had Allah willed He would have made one nation, with no rival groups to choose between; He chose not to compel anyone, into Islam or anything else.

outline.heading: Choice, and oaths driven by interest
outline.gist: His decree is that people choose; He lets astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. Do not let oaths and covenants be driven by corruption or the hunt for power and safety.

outline.heading: The foot that slips after standing firm
outline.gist: Changing loyalties out of interest, fear, greed or changed circumstances makes a foot that stood on principle slip, leaving only difficulty and distance from people and from Allah, with a great punishment.

outline.heading: Do not sell Allah's covenant for a small price
outline.gist: Do not give up the covenant for a cheap return; what is with Allah is better for you, and nothing else is.

outline.heading: What you hold runs out
outline.gist: Whatever you have, whatever it may be, will not last, because you yourself run out; nothing is worth more than holding to the covenant, which lasts forever because its source is the Divine.

outline.heading: What is with Allah remains
outline.gist: What is with Allah endures, and He will repay the patient by the best of what they did; then the promise to the believer, male or female, who does good.

outline.heading: A good life promised to the individual
outline.gist: Most of Allah's promises in this world are made to the collective; to the individual He promises only this, a good life, tayyibah from the root of goodness, and the best reward in the Hereafter.

outline.heading: Outro

32:2.ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
32:2.en: [This is] the revelation of the Book about which there is no doubt from the Lord of the worlds

32:3.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۚ بَلۡ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أَتَىٰهُم مِّن نَّذِيرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَهۡتَدُونَ
32:3.en: Or do they say, "He invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, [O Muhammad], that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you [so] perhaps they will be guided

31:15.ar: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفࣰ اۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
31:15.en: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do

24:55.ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَنَّهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَمَا ٱسۡتَخۡلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمۡ دِينَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي ٱرۡتَضَىٰ لَهُمۡ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَوۡفِهِمۡ أَمۡنࣰ اۚ يَعۡبُدُونَنِي لَا يُشۡرِكُونَ بِي شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:55.en: Allah has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession [to authority] upon the earth just as He granted it to those before them and that He will surely establish for them [therein] their religion which He has preferred for them and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient

16:97.ar: مَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوۡ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنࣱ فَلَنُحۡيِيَنَّهُۥ حَيَوٰةࣰ طَيِّبَةࣰۖ وَلَنَجۡزِيَنَّهُمۡ أَجۡرَهُم بِأَحۡسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
16:97.en: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do

2:96.ar: وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمۡ أَحۡرَصَ ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ حَيَوٰةࣲ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْۚ يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمۡ لَوۡ يُعَمَّرُ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحۡزِحِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ
2:96.en: And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life - [even] more than those who associate others with Allah. One of them wishes that he could be granted life a thousand years, but it would not remove him in the least from the [coming] punishment that he should be granted life.
