uuJlkVTsm84.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat As-Sajdah (Introduction, verses 1-3)
uuJlkVTsm84.one_line: Opening As-Sajdah: the surah closes the Quran's 'relationships' cluster with the most important one, the servant's relationship with Allah.
uuJlkVTsm84.summary: He opens Surat As-Sajdah, which the Prophet recited every Friday Fajr, by placing it at the end of a cluster running from Al-Qasas: relationships with people, with time, with the laws of creation, between generations, and finally with Allah. The word sajdah sums up that last relationship, which is a private secret of the heart. Like any relationship it can grow dull and mechanical, and it only holds when both sides invest; Allah has already given first, so the effort is now ours. He draws a practical rule: do not chase people who do not want you, except parents and the minimum due to kin. Happiness depends on relationships far more than comfort, as newcomers to Canada discover, and a sound relationship with Allah repairs all the others. The only worldly promise to an individual in the Quran is a good life, meaning inner fullness, not wealth or long life, which is why a barefoot child in Gaza has more dignity than the powerful who oppress him. He then explains his method of giving a compass for reflection, touches on the disjointed letters, and reads verses 1-3: revelation is Allah communicating, the relationship needs certainty with no doubt, and its purpose is guidance.

outline.heading: The Prophet's Friday Fajr recitation of As-Sajdah
outline.gist: He recited As-Sajdah and Al-Insan in full every Friday Fajr and prostrated in it, a sunnah the companions kept constantly.

outline.heading: The cluster of surahs on relationships
outline.gist: From Al-Qasas to As-Sajdah each surah treats one relationship: people, time, the laws of creation, generations, and lastly Allah.

outline.heading: Why sajdah sums up the relationship with Allah
outline.gist: Prostration of body, heart and mind captures the bond; unlike other relationships it is a hidden secret between the servant and his Lord.

outline.heading: When the relationship grows dull and mechanical
outline.gist: Relationships fluctuate; do not curse time, and beware of speaking to Allah with the tongue while the heart wanders. The dullness comes from our side, never His.

outline.heading: Both sides must invest, and Allah gave first
outline.gist: His nearness, love and pleasure match ours; He has already shown kindness through countless blessings, including bringing you to His house tonight.

outline.heading: The son of Adam who insults and repels his Lord
outline.gist: The hadith qudsi on people reviling Allah and making themselves hateful to Him through sin despite His favours shows a relationship only one side is mending.

outline.heading: Do not chase those who do not want you, except parents and kin
outline.gist: Parents are honoured regardless and kinship is kept at least at a minimum; otherwise leave people who reject you. A marriage also needs both spouses to want it.

outline.heading: Everything in the deen is this relationship
outline.gist: Prayer, dua, striving, obedience and sin are all the content of the bond with Allah; some surahs address such central topics more directly than others.

outline.heading: Surahs the Prophet kept reciting and the virtue of Friday
outline.gist: Al-Kahf, Al-Mulk, As-Sajdah and Al-Insan were recited regularly, a signal to pay close attention; Friday's merits explain why he started it with this surah.

outline.heading: Relationships are the secret of happiness
outline.gist: Newcomers to Canada have every comfort yet feel miserable because they lack family and friends; a king is lonely because he has only followers and rivals.

outline.heading: A sound relationship with Allah repairs every other one
outline.gist: Honouring parents, accepting hard laws of creation and bearing people all become acts of obedience to Him, so those close to Allah are content even in war and poverty.

outline.heading: Quality of life, not length or wealth
outline.gist: As medicine weighs quality of life against extra months, what matters is how one lives; people wrongly measure it by money, fame or career.

outline.heading: The only worldly promise to the individual: a good life
outline.gist: Promises to the community exist, but to the individual Allah promises only a good life, not health, wealth, children or protection from persecution.

outline.heading: What 'tayyib' means: a life filled from within
outline.gist: Like fruit that ripens when filled with water and sugar, a good life has no inner emptiness because one knows why he exists and accepts trials as tests.

outline.heading: Dignity of the oppressed in Gaza versus the fear of the oppressor
outline.gist: The powerful occupier lives afraid and mocked, while a barefoot child in Gaza is more honoured because he stands with truth; Abu Bakr told the Prophet he was good in life and death.

outline.heading: The relationship with Allah is a private secret
outline.gist: No one knows another's bond with Allah; Abu Bakr was distinguished by something settled in his heart, and those who know Allah recognise one another.

outline.heading: The method of these sessions: a compass for reflection
outline.gist: He leaves grammar and fiqh to the classical tafsirs and aims to show each surah's purpose so listeners can reflect correctly on their own, as his teachers sought insights even from students.

outline.heading: Alif Lam Mim as a thread linking surahs
outline.gist: The disjointed letters group surahs that share a theme; each surah has dimensions of revelation time, place in the mushaf, and what it gives you.

outline.heading: Revelation as Allah speaking to you
outline.gist: No relationship exists without communication; besides what He gives and takes in life, Allah addressed us directly by sending down a Book.

outline.heading: No doubt in it: certainty as the foundation
outline.gist: The relationship cannot stand if one doubts Allah or that the Book is His word; one must know who the other party is and accept His speech.

outline.heading: Answering the claim that he fabricated it
outline.gist: The verse confronts doubts spread by the weak of faith: it is the truth from your Lord.

outline.heading: The purpose of the relationship: guidance
outline.gist: Every relationship needs a defined aim; this one is so that people may be guided, and the Arabs had received no warner for centuries.

outline.heading: Outro

32:4.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ مَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ مِن وَلِيࣲّ وَلَا شَفِيعٍۚ أَفَلَا تَتَذَكَّرُونَ
32:4.en: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or any intercessor; so will you not be reminded

32:5.ar: يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ثُمَّ يَعۡرُجُ إِلَيۡهِ فِي يَوۡمࣲ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥٓ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ
32:5.en: He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count

32:6.ar: ذَٰلِكَ عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
32:6.en: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Merciful

32:7.ar: ٱلَّذِيٓ أَحۡسَنَ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقَهُۥۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلۡقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ مِن طِينࣲ‏
32:7.en: Who perfected everything which He created and began the creation of man from clay

32:8.ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلَ نَسۡلَهُۥ مِن سُلَٰلَةࣲ مِّن مَّآءࣲ مَّهِينࣲ‏
32:8.en: Then He made his posterity out of the extract of a liquid disdained

32:9.ar: ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦۖ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَٱلۡأَفۡـِٔدَةَۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
32:9.en: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful

32:2.ar: تَنزِيلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا رَيۡبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
32:2.en: [This is] the revelation of the Book about which there is no doubt from the Lord of the worlds

32:3.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ ٱفۡتَرَىٰهُۚ بَلۡ هُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ لِتُنذِرَ قَوۡمࣰ ا مَّآ أَتَىٰهُم مِّن نَّذِيرࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِكَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَهۡتَدُونَ
32:3.en: Or do they say, "He invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, [O Muhammad], that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you [so] perhaps they will be guided

36:82.ar: إِنَّمَآ أَمۡرُهُۥٓ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيۡـًٔا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ

35:15.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ أَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱللَّهُ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ

7:54.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ يَطۡلُبُهُۥ حَثِيثࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَٰتِۭ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۗ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ وَٱلۡأَمۡرُۗ تَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:54.en: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, [another night] chasing it rapidly; and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds

70:4.ar: تَعۡرُجُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيۡهِ فِي يَوۡمࣲ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهُۥ خَمۡسِينَ أَلۡفَ سَنَةࣲ‏
70:4.en: The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years

2TpzEBFYHeg.speaker_note: the sheikh's Sunday Arabic tafsir; he recounts going to the masjid the night the Syrian regime fell and refers to problems brought to him at the masjid
2TpzEBFYHeg.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat As-Sajdah (verses 4-9)
2TpzEBFYHeg.one_line: Allah introduces Himself before asking anything: Creator, independent on the Throne, sole protector and intercessor, Knower, Mighty and Merciful, then reminds us to be grateful.
2TpzEBFYHeg.summary: He begins with the night the Syrian regime fell, when he found no one to turn to but Allah and went to the masjid. The lesson: in joy or calamity the first reflex should be returning to Allah, in prostration of gratitude or patience, before celebrating with people. Empty masjids mean empty hearts, and a revival of the ummah will only come when hearts are attached to Allah. He then explains verses 4-9. Allah speaks about Himself first: He created the heavens and earth in six of His days, which are spans of time, not ours. Rising over the Throne signals that He needs nothing; He did not create us for any need, which makes this relationship unique. There is no protector or intercessor besides Him, so the culture of connections and middlemen that people love in worldly life has no place with Allah, not even through the Prophet. He distinguishes what Allah decrees from what humans choose, the deeds that rise back to Him. The names Knower of the unseen and seen, Mighty and Merciful lay the foundations of the bond. He perfected all creation and made opposites so we can recognise beauty. Having given us hearing, sight and understanding, the painful verdict is that we are little grateful.

outline.heading: The night the Syrian regime fell
outline.gist: Overwhelmed by sudden relief after years of oppression, he realised the only one to turn to was Allah and went to sit in the masjid.

outline.heading: The first reflex in joy or calamity: return to Allah
outline.gist: Before celebrating or complaining to people, prostrate in gratitude or in patience, praise Him and seek forgiveness, then thank those who were a means.

outline.heading: Empty masjids, empty hearts
outline.gist: People once brought every piece of news to the masjid; when the houses of Allah emptied, hearts emptied. The next day the masjid filled spontaneously with people praising Allah.

outline.heading: Visiting Allah in His house
outline.gist: As a relationship with parents means visiting them, a relationship with Allah means coming to His house; the believer's heart is attached to the masjid.

outline.heading: Share your joy with Allah before your friends
outline.gist: When good news comes, go to Allah first, then go out, feed people and fulfil your vows.

outline.heading: Darkness before dawn: revival needs hearts attached to Allah
outline.gist: He prays for oppressed Muslim lands and argues an enslaved, ignorant nation cannot rise; the change comes when young and old attach their hearts to Allah.

outline.heading: Why Friday Fajr: the Muslim week starts with Jumuah
outline.gist: The week begins on Friday, and opening it with this surah ties the heart to Allah for the whole week.

outline.heading: Recap: revelation, certainty and guidance
outline.gist: The relationship starts with His speech; He spoke to us before we spoke to Him, without doubt, so that we may be guided.

outline.heading: He speaks of Himself first: Creator of heavens and earth
outline.gist: Before describing what He wants from us, Allah tells us who He is; 'sky' covers everything that is not the earth we stand on.

outline.heading: Six days: His days, not ours
outline.gist: A day is a span of time set by the speaker; scholars read the six as long eras or as night, day and the four seasons. He needs no time, but creation needed time to mature, like the earth cooling.

outline.heading: We are a tiny part of His creation
outline.gist: The verse places us as a small piece within an immense cosmos.

outline.heading: Rising over the Throne: affirming without likening
outline.gist: One may leave its meaning to Allah or interpret it as dominion; Ahl al-Sunnah differ on this, and every position seeks to declare Him free of resemblance to creation.

outline.heading: He created us without needing us
outline.gist: Unlike an employer who hires because he needs workers, Allah gains nothing from us; even our worship benefits only us, making this relationship unlike any other.

outline.heading: Loyalty to the One who made you from nothing
outline.gist: A person is less than a dot in a fourteen-billion-year cosmos; if he cannot love and thank the One who brought him into being, what good is in him?

outline.heading: No protector or intercessor besides Him
outline.gist: Everything returns to Allah, so do not look for anyone else; even the Prophet is your teacher, not a channel you speak to Allah through.

outline.heading: Will you not remember? People keep making idols
outline.gist: After every messenger people forget and fashion idols of stone or of human authorities again.

outline.heading: The culture of connections has no place with Allah
outline.gist: People love skipping the queue through someone they know; whatever one thinks of it in worldly life, anyone claiming to broker your affairs with Allah is a liar.

outline.heading: He directs the affair; a day of a thousand years
outline.gist: Creation and command belong to Him; the Quran's 'day' can be a thousand or fifty thousand years, which the Arabs understood.

outline.heading: His decree versus human choice
outline.gist: What He directs is His decree beyond our control, such as illness and death; the wars and greed of humans are their own choices. Our deeds in response to His decree are what rise to Him.

outline.heading: Recitation of the next passage
outline.gist: He reads the verses on the Knower of the unseen and the creation of man.

outline.heading: Knower of the unseen and the seen
outline.gist: Nothing escapes Him, seen or hidden, so you need not fear that any detail is lost.

outline.heading: Al-Aziz: beyond our questioning
outline.gist: We lack the tools to grasp why He creates, as a four-year-old cannot understand marriage; asking Him to justify Himself is futile.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahim, and the three names as foundations
outline.gist: Though Mighty, He is merciful toward our curiosity, weakness and desires; knowing, mighty and merciful together ground the relationship.

outline.heading: He perfected everything He created
outline.gist: Ihsan is doing a thing with full care; the reflective person comes to see beauty in everything, while Satan points only at defects.

outline.heading: Opposites make blessings visible
outline.gist: Without sourness, ugliness, poverty and illness we could not value sweetness, beauty, wealth and health; a spoiled child is ungrateful while an orphan from the tents of Gaza is thankful for water.

outline.heading: Your own creation: clay, a humble fluid, then His spirit
outline.gist: From the whole cosmos the verses turn to your personal story, from clay and a lowly fluid to being shaped and given spirit.

outline.heading: Tools of connection, and how little you thank
outline.gist: Hearing, sight and understanding are what make a relationship possible; the first flaw the surah names in our side of it is ingratitude.

outline.heading: Outro

stories.point: Sudden relief left him with nowhere to go but Allah's house; the next day the masjid filled spontaneously with praise.

stories.who: Problems brought to him at the masjid
stories.point: He tells people to send the matter straight to him rather than through others, a small image of all affairs ending with Allah.

stories.who: Skipping the queue through a connection
stories.point: The prestige of knowing someone in a government office is what people love, and exactly what does not exist with Allah.

stories.who: Explaining marriage to a four-year-old
stories.point: We lack the tools to understand Allah's reasons, as a small child cannot grasp adult matters.

stories.who: A spoiled child and an orphan from Gaza
stories.point: Only one who has known hardship recognises and thanks for blessings.

contemporary: Anniversary of the fall of the Assad regime in Syria
Oppression in Palestine, Egypt, Yemen, Iraq, Afghanistan, Libya and hunger in Sudan
Orphans in the tents of Gaza
Reliance on personal connections in government offices
takeaways: In good news or bad, go to Allah first: prostrate, praise and seek forgiveness before telling people
Make the masjid your second home and bring your joys and worries to it
Raise children whose hearts are attached to Allah; that is the path to revival
Deal with Allah directly; reject anyone claiming to broker your affairs with Him
Practise gratitude by noticing blessings against their opposites
